The Aztec Empire. The Mexica people established Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, developing a vast empire through military conquest and tributary networks that flourished from roughly thirteen hundred to fifteen twenty-one. The capital's population exceeded two hundred thousand by the early fifteen hundreds, rivaling Europe's largest cities with sophisticated canals, aqueducts, and floating gardens. When Hernán Cortés arrived in fifteen nineteen, Emperor Montezuma's initial diplomatic hesitation gave the Spanish time to consolidate alliances with indigenous rivals and exploit internal divisions.
